mainTopic: Acquiring many fields with one חזקה, and the תורה source for גלגול שבועה
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא. Taking possession (חזקה) of one field acquires all the fields in the sale, but only if the buyer paid for all of them. The גמרא says this supports שמואל, who rules that ten fields in ten different places are all acquired through a חזקה on one. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא compares the fields to ten animals tied to one bridle, first to support שמואל and, in a second version, to argue against him. Both comparisons are pushed away, and שמואל stands because all land counts as one connected mass. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that movables pull land into an oath. עולא brings the תורה source for גלגול שבועה from the סוטה's double 'אמן'. Her oath covers her time as an ארוסה, and the גמרא shows this can only work by extending an oath she already has to take. Finally, the גמרא asks how we know גלגול applies to money matters, and דבי רבי ישמעאל begins a קל וחומר from סוטה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The buyer only gets what he paid for
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its rule: one חזקה acquires all the fields only when the buyer paid for all of them. Otherwise he acquires only the amount his money covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this rule true? When he paid for all the fields. But if he did not pay for all of them, he acquires only as much as his money covers.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a limit to its earlier rule that a חזקה on one field acquires all of them. The rule only works if the buyer paid the full price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's rule was that a חזקה on one field acquires every field in the sale. Now it adds a condition: the buyer must have paid for everything. If he paid only part, the חזקה acquires only the share that his money covers.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (a phrase that introduces a limit on a rule)
The price, the money for something
Matching his money; only as much as he paid for

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא's rule that taking possession of one field acquires all the fields being sold.

phrases.english: When he gave him the money for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא נָתַן לוֹ דְּמֵי כוּלָּן –
phrases.english: but if he did not give him the money for all of them,
he acquires only as much as matches his money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that the earlier part of the daf was quoting
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה on one field acquires all the fields only if the buyer paid for all of them. Otherwise he acquires only the share his money covers.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא backs up שמואל, who rules that a חזקה on one of ten fields in ten different places acquires all ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports שמואל, because שמואל said: If someone sold another person ten fields in ten different places, once the buyer took possession of one of them, he acquires all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא we just learned agrees with a ruling of שמואל, and then quotes שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's חידוש is that the fields do not need to be next to each other. Even fields in ten different places are all acquired through a חזקה on one of them. The ברייתא says the same thing, so it serves as a support for שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: This supports him
Places, regions
He took possession (made a חֲזָקָה), for example by doing work on the field
He acquired

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule that the rest of the section argues about: can one act of חזקה acquire land that is far away?

phrases.english: This supports שמואל,
for שמואל said:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר לוֹ עֶשֶׂר שָׂדוֹת בְּעֶשֶׂר מְדִינוֹת,
phrases.english: If he sold him ten fields in ten different places,
once he took possession of one of them,
he acquires all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 1 as a support for שמואל
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a חזקה on one field acquires ten fields in ten different places
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, which rules the same way

steps.title: רב אחא proves שמואל right with ten animals on one bridle
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא supports שמואל from a case of ten animals tied to one bridle. If the seller hands over the bridle and says 'acquire', the buyer gets all ten animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: You can see this is true. If someone handed another person ten animals on one bridle and told him 'Acquire', wouldn't he acquire all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא brings a logical proof for שמואל from a case everyone agrees on: ten animals on one bridle are all acquired together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Handing over one bridle acquires all ten animals, even though the buyer only holds one thing. רב אחא argues that the ten fields work the same way: a חזקה on one field brings in all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: You should know; a phrase that introduces a proof from logic or from a known case
A bridle, the rope or strap used to lead an animal
He handed over
Acquire! (the seller telling the buyer to take ownership)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא son of רב איקא said:
Know that this is so, for if he handed him
ten animals with one bridle
and said to him, 'Acquire',
doesn't he acquire them?

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּדַע, שֶׁאִילּוּ מָסַר לוֹ עֶשֶׂר בְּהֵמוֹת בְּאַפְסָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a logical proof for שמואל's ruling from step 2
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that one חזקה acquires all ten fields
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to ten animals on one bridle, which are all acquired together

steps.title: The bridle case is different: it ties everything together
steps.stepSummary: Someone rejects רב אחא's comparison. The bridle physically connects the animals, and the buyer holds it in his hand. The ten fields have no such connector.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is that the same? There, the thing that ties them together is in his hand. Here, the thing that ties them together is not in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: An unnamed person rejects רב אחא's proof and says the animal case is not like the field case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the animals, the bridle is a real physical tie (איגודו), and the buyer is holding it, so all ten come along. The fields in ten different places have nothing holding them together in the buyer's hand. So the bridle case cannot prove שמואל right.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it the same? (a phrase that introduces a rejection of a comparison)
The thing that ties them together
There / here

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it comparable?
There, the thing tying them together is in his hand,
phrases.notes: He means the bridle, which joins all ten animals.

phrases.english: here, the thing tying them together is not in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב אחא's proof is rejected; שמואל's ruling itself still stands
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bridle physically ties the animals together in the buyer's hand, and the scattered fields have no such tie
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רב אחא's bridle proof for שמואל fails, because the bridle is a physical connector and the fields have none.

steps.title: Second version: רב אחא argues the buyer does not acquire all the fields
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב אחא uses the bridle case against שמואל. If the seller says 'acquire this one', the buyer does not get all ten animals, so a חזקה on one field should not acquire all the fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: You can see that he does not acquire. If someone handed another person ten animals on one bridle and said 'Acquire this one', would he acquire all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רב אחא said. In this report he argues against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the seller points to one animal and says 'acquire this one', so only that animal is acquired. Taking possession of one field is like saying 'acquire this one', so the other fields should not be acquired. This is the reverse of the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: This one

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the same bridle case, but they point in opposite directions. In version one, the seller says 'acquire' and all the animals are acquired, which supports שמואל. In version two, he says 'acquire this one' and they are not all acquired, which goes against שמואל.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא son of רב איקא said:
Know that he does not acquire,

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ מָסַר לוֹ עֶשֶׂר בְּהֵמוֹת בְּאַפְסָר אֶחָד
phrases.english: for if he handed him ten animals with one bridle
and said to him, 'Acquire this one',
does he acquire them?
phrases.notes: This question expects the answer 'no, he does not acquire all of them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: תֵּדַע דְּלָא קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב אחא's statement, using the same bridle case to argue against שמואל
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a חזקה on one field does not acquire the other fields
steps.raayaSupportSource: Ten animals on one bridle, where the seller said 'acquire this one'

steps.title: Animals are separate, but all land is one mass
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second version as well. Animals are separate bodies, but all the earth is one connected mass, so a חזקה on one field can reach the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that the same? There, they are separate bodies. Here, the ground of the earth is all one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אחא's argument against שמואל and shows why land is different from animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal is its own separate body, so 'acquire this one' covers only that animal. Land is different: all the earth counts as one connected mass. That means fields far apart are still joined, and a חזקה on one can acquire them all, just as שמואל ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate bodies, things that are not joined
The block or mass of the earth; all land seen as one connected piece
It is one

steps.whatToRemember: All land is one connected mass (סדנא דארעא חד הוא). That is why a חזקה on one field can acquire fields in other places, which defends שמואל's ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of סדנא דארעא חד הוא explains how one act of חזקה on land can work for fields that are far apart.

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There, they are separate bodies,
here, the mass of the earth is one.
phrases.notes: Even fields in different places are all part of one ground, so they count as connected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second version of רב אחא's argument from step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The argument against שמואל is rejected completely, so שמואל's ruling stands
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Animals are separate bodies, while all land is one connected mass
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's ruling stands: because all land is connected, a חזקה on one field can acquire fields in other places.

steps.title: Where does the תורה teach that an oath can be extended?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that movables bind land into an oath. עולא asks for the תורה source of גלגול שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they bind the property, etc.' עולא says: From where do we know from the תורה that an oath can be extended to other claims?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. עולא asks where the תורה teaches that one oath can 'roll' onto other claims, and he will answer it himself in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if someone must swear about movables, he can be made to swear about land too, even though land alone never brings an oath. That only works if the תורה allows a required oath to pull in other claims. עולא is asking for the source of that idea, called גלגול שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: Bind or pull along. Movables 'pull' the land into the oath.
Rolling an oath. Once someone must swear on one matter, other matters can be added to his oath.
From where? A request for a source.

phrases.english: And they bind the property, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: movable property pulls the land along, so someone swearing about the movables swears about the land too.

phrases.english: Ulla says:
From where is the extension of an oath derived
from the Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of חזקה on many fields and turns to a new line of the משנה about oaths.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The תורה source for גלגול שבועה

steps.title: The double 'אמן' of the סוטה covers more than the original suspicion
steps.stepSummary: עולא brings the פסוק 'ואמרה האשה אמן אמן'. A משנה explains that the doubled אמן extends the סוטה's oath to other men and to other periods of her life.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And the woman shall say: Amen, amen.' And we learned in a משנה: On what does she say 'Amen, amen'? 'Amen' on the curse, 'Amen' on the oath. 'Amen' if from this man, 'Amen' if from another man. 'Amen' that I did not stray while betrothed, while married, while waiting for the יבם, or after the יבם married me.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers his own question with the oath of the סוטה. The משנה shows that her 'אמן' covers more than the one man and the one time she was suspected about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists things her oath covers beyond the immediate suspicion, including stages of her life such as her time as an ארוסה. עולא's proof will rest on the ארוסה part. The next steps show that her betrothal period can only enter her oath by being added onto an oath she already has to take, which is גלגול שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife who was warned by her husband and then secluded herself with another man. She is tested with the bitter water.
The curse that comes on her if she is guilty
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום
Taken in, meaning married to the יבם through יבום

steps.whatToRemember: The סוטה's oath also covers her time as an ארוסה. The next steps show that this can only work through גלגול, which makes it the תורה model for גלגול שבועה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the משנה's rule that movables can pull land into an oath. A required oath can carry other claims with it.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And the woman shall say: Amen, amen,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:22. This is the woman suspected as a סוטה.

phrases.english: and we learned in a mishna:
Concerning what does she say "Amen, amen"?
"Amen" on the curse,
"Amen" on the oath.
"Amen" if I sinned with this man,
"Amen" if I sinned with another man.
"Amen" that I did not stray
when betrothed or when married,
or while waiting for my yavam, or once taken in by him.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled אמן of the סוטה, as the משנה explains it, includes her time as an ארוסה. Steps 9-13 show that this can only work through גלגול, so it is the source for גלגול שבועה.

steps.title: How could an ארוסה be part of the סוטה's oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means by 'ארוסה'. It first suggests she was warned and given the water to drink while still betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This betrothed woman, what is the case? If we say he warned her while she was betrothed and gives her the water to drink while she is betrothed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the betrothed-woman part of the משנה works. It offers a first, simple answer, which it is setting up to attack in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says she swears she did not stray 'as an ארוסה', but it does not say how her betrothal became part of the test. The first suggestion is that the whole process happened while she was betrothed: the warning, and the drinking too.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
If we say. It introduces a suggestion that will usually be rejected.
He warned her (קינוי) not to be alone with a certain man
He has her drink the bitter water

phrases.english: This betrothed woman, what are the circumstances?
If we say that he warned her when she was betrothed,
and he gives her the water to drink when she is betrothed,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the word ארוסה in the משנה quoted in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case does the סוטה's oath cover her time as an ארוסה?

steps.title: A betrothed woman never drinks the bitter water
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion fails. A משנה teaches that an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם do not drink, because the פסוק says 'תחת אישך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: A betrothed woman and a widow waiting for her יבם neither drink nor collect their כתובה? What is the reason? The Merciful One said 'under your husband,' and that is not the case here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from step 9. A betrothed woman cannot be given the water at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a woman who strayed 'under your husband', meaning a fully married wife. An ארוסה is not yet living under her husband, so she cannot drink. That means the משנה's ארוסה cannot be a woman tested while still betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: Under your husband, meaning while you are fully married to him
It is not there; that condition is missing

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
A betrothed woman and a widow waiting for her yavam
neither drink nor collect their marriage contract?
What is the reason?
The Merciful One said "under your husband,"
and that is not the case here.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן אֲרוּסָה וְשׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם לֹא שׁוֹתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first suggestion offered in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the ארוסה was warned and drank while still betrothed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that an ארוסה never drinks, because the פסוק requires 'תחת אישך'. So that case cannot be what the משנה means.

steps.title: Warned and secluded while betrothed, but drinks after marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new case. He warned her and she secluded herself while she was betrothed, but she drinks only once she is married.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he warned her when she was betrothed, and she secluded herself when she was betrothed, and he gives her the water to drink when she is married...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the rejected case with a new one. The next step challenges this new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the drinking happens when she is fully married, so 'תחת אישך' is satisfied. The warning and the seclusion, though, took place back during her betrothal. This explains how her betrothal period becomes part of the oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It brings a new answer after the first one was rejected.
She secluded herself, meaning she was alone with the man she was warned about
Fully married (after נישואין)

phrases.english: Rather, he warned her when she was betrothed,
and she secluded herself when she was betrothed,
and he gives her the water to drink when she is married,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקַנִּי לַהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא אֲרוּסָה וְנִסְתְּרָה כְּשֶׁהִיא אֲרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10 by moving the drinking to after the marriage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ארוסה was warned and also drank while betrothed.
steps.terutzMaskana: She was warned and secluded while betrothed, but drinks only after marriage. That satisfies 'תחת אישך'.

steps.title: The water would not test her anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the case from step 11. The פסוק 'ונקה האיש מעון' teaches that the water tests the wife only when the husband is free of sin. Here the husband lived with her while she was forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But would the water really test her? The תורה says, 'And the man shall be clean from sin.' This teaches that when the husband is clean from sin, the water tests his wife. When the husband is not clean from sin, the water does not test his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the case from step 11, where she was warned and secluded herself as an ארוסה and drank only after the marriage. It argues the water could not work in that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she secluded herself after a warning, she became forbidden to her husband until she drinks. If he married her and lived with her anyway, he sinned. The פסוק says the water only works when the husband is free of sin, so this case cannot produce a real test.

keyTerms.meaning: The water tests her. This refers to the bitter water that proves whether a סוטה sinned.
'And the man shall be clean from sin' (במדבר ה:לא).
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ that is used when quoting the Torah.
Clean from sin. Here it means the husband did not sin in matters of forbidden relations.

steps.confusionAlert: The husband's sin here is not some unrelated sin. He lived with her while she was forbidden to him because of her seclusion. That specific sin is why the water would not work.

phrases.english: Does the water test her?
phrases.notes: He means the case from step 11: warned and secluded as an ארוסה, but drinking only after the marriage.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said: 'And the man shall be clean from sin.'
When the man is clean from sin,
the water tests his wife;
when the man is not clean from sin,
phrases.notes: After her seclusion she was forbidden to him. By marrying her and living with her, he sinned.

phrases.english: the water does not test his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case proposed in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case from step 11: she was warned and secluded herself as an ארוסה and drank after the marriage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband sinned by living with his forbidden wife. Under 'ונקה האיש מעון', the water does not test her, so the case cannot work.

steps.title: The betrothal period is included through גלגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ארוסה period in the משנה is not a case of drinking for that period. It is added to her oath only by גלגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the oath about the betrothal period comes in by being rolled in with her other oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on finding a case where she drinks because of the ארוסה period. Instead, it says that period is added to her oath through גלגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband could not make her drink only about her time as an ארוסה. But once she must drink and swear about her married life, her oath can be extended to cover the betrothal period too. This makes the doubled אמן a clear source for גלגול שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: By means of rolling it in. A matter that could not bring an oath on its own is added to an oath she already has to take.

steps.whatToRemember: The סוטה's oath covering her time as an ארוסה works only through גלגול. That is why the פסוק of 'אמן אמן' is the תורה source for גלגול שבועה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This locks in עולא's proof from step 8. The ארוסה case can only be explained as a גלגול, so the פסוק really does teach גלגול שבועה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is by means of extension!
phrases.notes: Her oath about her married life drags along an oath about the time she was betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes how the case works: it is a גלגול, not an independent drinking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She might drink because of what happened during the betrothal itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The betrothal period is covered only by extending her required oath about her married life.

steps.title: What about money cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the סוטה source only shows גלגול in a matter of איסור. It asks for a source for גלגול in money matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for סוטה, which is a matter of prohibition. How do we know it for money matters?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has a source for גלגול in the case of סוטה. Now it asks how we know the same rule applies to money matters, which is what our משנה is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוטה is a matter of איסור, a forbidden relationship. Our משנה applies גלגול to money claims about property and land. So the גמרא needs a way to carry the rule from איסור over to ממון.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found a source for this.
A matter of prohibition, about what is forbidden or permitted.
A money matter.
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We found it for a סוטה, which is a matter of prohibition;
from where do we know it for money matters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the source found in steps 8 to 13 and asks to extend it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that גלגול שבועה applies in money matters, not only in matters of איסור.

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל begins a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל answers with a קל וחומר that starts from the case of סוטה. The argument continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: it is a קל וחומר. If in the case of a סוטה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. דבי רבי ישמעאל will learn money matters from סוטה through a קל וחומר, and the argument continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר reasons that if a rule applies in one case, it surely applies in another case where there is more reason for it. The opening words 'ומה סוטה' show that סוטה is the starting case. The full comparison comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall of רבי ישמעאל taught.
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one.
'And if…', the usual opening of a קל וחומר.
